citation: Ansari, A., & Pianta, R. C. (2018). Effects of an early childhood educator coaching intervention on preschoolers: The role of classroom age composition. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 44, 101-113. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2018.03.001
report_number: Journal article (no IES/NCEE/EEF report number). DOI: 10.1016/j.ecresq.2018.03.001. Secondary moderation/mediation analysis of the NCRECE Teacher Professional Development Study, the MyTeachingPartner (MTP) web-mediated coaching RCT (UVA CASTL). Funding: IES R305B130013; AERA/NSF DRL-0941014.
design: Cluster-RCT, assignment at the Teacher/Class level within site (business-as-usual control). MyTeachingPartner (MTP) web-mediated coaching PD intervention vs control. Pre-K (Head Start + public pre-K), 9 urban sites in 8 states, 2 cohorts. Analytic sample for this paper: 325 teachers/classrooms (168 MTP, 157 control) and 1407 four-year-old children (736 MTP, 671 control). Outcomes: early language/literacy (Reading) + inhibitory control (executive function, not achievement). No math/STEM outcome measured. Models: covariate-adjusted regression in Mplus, clustered at classroom level, site fixed effects, lagged (pretest) dependent variables; all variables standardized so coefficients = effect sizes.
problems: This is a secondary MODERATION/MODERATED-MEDIATION analysis (focus: classroom age composition as a moderator), NOT a primary impact report. HOWEVER it does report a clean main-effect TPD-vs-control contrast: Table 2 'Main effect model' row gives the average MTP-coaching treatment effect for each of 5 standardized child outcomes, with SEs, from the covariate-adjusted classroom-clustered model (note: 'all continuous variables standardized... all parameter estimates correspond to effect sizes'). These standardized coefficients are used directly as Hedges' g (after the J small-sample correction, which is ~0.9995 and negligible at N=1407). None of the main effects is statistically significant (overall MTP ES ~= 0.03 SD, ns). Limitations/ambiguities: (1) The exact df for each model's standardizing SD is not given; J computed from total N-2 = 1405. (2) Variance: g_se = J * reported SE(d) (the model SEs already account for classroom clustering -> cluster_adjusted=true; n_clusters=325; ICC not reported -> left null, NEVER guessed). (3) Only language/literacy outcomes map to achievement (Reading); inhibitory control is executive function/self-regulation, NOT academic achievement, and is EXCLUDED per spec. (4) No math or science outcome exists in this study, so there is NO STEM contrast. (5) The 'Average of all child outcomes' composite includes the non-achievement inhibitory-control measure, so it is recorded as a composite but is not a pure achievement composite (flagged in notes). (6) Table 1 also reports raw end-of-year posttest means/SDs by group (unadjusted, not pretest-adjusted) which corroborate the near-null differences; the Table 2 adjusted standardized coefficients are preferred and used for g.
